message.content: Lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) are both placental mammals, but they belong to different orders—Carnivora for lions and Perissodactyla for zebras. Their most recent common ancestor is therefore a small, early Laurasiatherian mammal that lived roughly 70–80 million years ago during the late Cretaceous/early Paleogene. This ancestor was a relatively simple, insect‑eating mammal that gave rise to the diverse lineages that eventually led to modern carnivores, perissodactyls, artiodactyls, bats, and cetaceans.
